“We didn’t fight in Liberation War to be labelled as minority”
2022-10-01T22:25:17+06:00 | Star Digital Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/we-didnt-fight-liberation-war-be-labelled-minority-3132726

Bangladesh Puja Udjapon Parishad President JL Bhowmik today (October 1, 2022) said they did not fight take part in Liberation War to be identified as a minority community. "This thinking is against the spirit of the country's constitution of 1972."

Bhowmik said this at a view exchange meeting with the newly elected leaders of the Religious Reporters Forum (RRF) held at Dhakeshwari Mandir in the capital.

The leaders of Bangladesh Puja Udjapon Parishad and Dhaka Mohanagar Sarbojonin Puja Committee called for increasing communal harmony in the country and asked for everyone's cooperation to ensure proper management of puja celebrations across the country.

The parishad president General Secretary and Dhaka University Prof Chandranath Poddar said the current government is working for the development of minorities, but it is very less compared to the total population.

He urged Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to remove this discrimination.

RRF President Ubaidullah Badal and General Secretary Kamruzzaman Bablu led the delegation on behalf of the organisation.

Mahanagar Sarvajanin Puja Committee President Monindra Kumar Nath, former president and former secretary Shailendranath Majumder, adviser Jayanta Sen Dipu, were present at the time among others.
